angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 389,592 km at 100.96 pc = 0.05 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 9.9046 +/- 0.0242 mas (same row, RUWE 1.06): 100.96 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.56 +/- 0.03 solar radii from Mann et al. 2022, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-1227 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163..156M/abstract): 389,592 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.17 +/- 0.015 solar masses from Mann et al. 2022, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-1227 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163..156M/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3072 +/- 74 K from Mann et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1227 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163..156M/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Mann et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1227 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163..156M/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-1227.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.172, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
